commit_message:
[Stream] Fix O(N²) compile-time scaling in partitionRegionConcurrency (#24958)

When analyzing execution regions where many operations share a common
resource operand, `partitionRegionConcurrencyReference` previously
invoked `tiedOp.hasAnyTiedUses(operand)` inside the `operand.getUsers()`
loop. Because checking whether an operand has tied uses involves
scanning its use sites, repeating this check inside the loop caused
quadratic $O(N^2)$ traversal over the users of that operand.

This change hoists the check out of the loop using the static helper
`IREE::Util::TiedOpInterface::hasAnyTiedUses(operand)` as an early exit.
Inside the loop, it now only checks whether the candidate user
implements `TiedOpInterface`. This eliminates redundant scans and
resolves the compiler performance bottleneck while preserving existing
partitioning semantics.

Fixes #24928

  Signed-off-by: @isa-Lai 
  Assisted-by:  Gemini CLI

Signed-off-by: isa-lai <isabellai1004@gmail.com>

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a98f7ed68e (#24963)

LLVM staging branch: `sm-iree-integrates/llvm-20260925`

Adds a cherry-pick of llvm/llvm-project#226903 to support
minimumnumf/maximumnumf semantics. The new reduction kinds were
introduced in llvm/llvm-project@8306f777. QNaN was chosen as an identity
arg for the new kinds so as to propagate signalling NaNs correctly. As
per the LLVM LangRef:

> Return the other argument if one of the arguments is NaN.


(https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#floating-point-min-max-intrinsics-comparison)

Additionally:
- Update compiler and end-to-end TOSA tests for the strict property
assembly format (llvm/llvm-project@b9da7a34)
- Redeclare LLVM libxml2 and xz Bazel dependencies
(llvm/llvm-project@bd0da2bf7dae, llvm/llvm-project@4989b3b0)
- Regenerate API exports

Assisted-by: Codex

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
name: Tag candidate release

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Propagate QDQ before im2col conversion

Move quantization through layout operations before the early integer
contraction rewrite. Padded convolutions otherwise become im2col
packing operations before their dequantize producers can be matched.

Keep the later propagation run for reshapes and transposes introduced
by intervening passes, and cover eligible padded convolutions in the
production pipeline test.
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[Torch] Preserve PT2E quantization as LinalgExt ops

Convert the typed PT2E per-tensor and per-channel quantize and
dequantize operations before Torch-to-Linalg expands them. This keeps
affine parameter maps, ranges, and signedness available to later QDQ
optimizations.

Leave operations with dynamic or incompatible metadata for the
existing torch-mlir lowering.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

Move quantize operations toward real-valued producers and dequantize
operations toward contraction consumers before rewriting contractions to
integer math.

Reuse reshape expansion and unit-dimension folding for affine QDQ
operations. Handle transpose and zero-pad consumers using explicit
legality checks.

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@a98f7ed68e (#24963)

LLVM staging branch: `sm-iree-integrates/llvm-20260925`

Adds a cherry-pick of llvm/llvm-project#226903 to support
minimumnumf/maximumnumf semantics. The new reduction kinds were
introduced in llvm/llvm-project@8306f777. QNaN was chosen as an identity
arg for the new kinds so as to propagate signalling NaNs correctly. As
per the LLVM LangRef:

> Return the other argument if one of the arguments is NaN.


(https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#floating-point-min-max-intrinsics-comparison)

Additionally:
- Update compiler and end-to-end TOSA tests for the strict property
assembly format (llvm/llvm-project@b9da7a34)
- Redeclare LLVM libxml2 and xz Bazel dependencies
(llvm/llvm-project@bd0da2bf7dae, llvm/llvm-project@4989b3b0)
- Regenerate API exports

Assisted-by: Codex

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
name: linux_x64_gcc

Adds a cherry-pick of llvm/llvm-project#226903 to support
minimumnumf/maximumnumf semantics. The new reduction kinds were
introduced in llvm/llvm-project@8306f777. QNaN was chosen as an identity
arg for the new kinds so as to propagate signalling NaNs correctly. As
per the LLVM LangRef:

> Return the other argument if one of the arguments is NaN.


(https://llvm.org/docs/LangRef.html#floating-point-min-max-intrinsics-comparison)

Additionally:
- Update compiler and end-to-end TOSA tests for the strict property
assembly format (llvm/llvm-project@b9da7a34)
- Redeclare LLVM libxml2 and xz Bazel dependencies
(llvm/llvm-project@bd0da2bf7dae, llvm/llvm-project@4989b3b0)
- Regenerate API exports

Assisted-by: Codex

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Unify measurement and dispatch profiling

Use the same batch lifecycle for measurement and untimed profiling so sync,
async, and generated dispatch benchmarks preserve their iteration accounting
and concurrency. Keep execution out of reporters and share profiling session
ownership and cleanup across all participating devices.

Retain asynchronous outputs, normalize dispatch rows across repetitions, and
include them in both display and file reports. Return recording devices from
context setup so async fences participate in replay capture.

Cover reporting, output ownership, batch semantics, multi-device capture, and
failure cleanup with lifecycle tests.

Use the same batch lifecycle for measurement and untimed profiling so sync,
async, and generated dispatch benchmarks preserve their iteration accounting
and concurrency. Keep execution out of reporters and share profiling session
ownership and cleanup across all participating devices.

Retain asynchronous outputs, normalize dispatch rows across repetitions, and
include them in both display and file reports. Return recording devices from
context setup so async fences participate in replay capture.

Cover reporting, output ownership, batch semantics, multi-device capture, and
failure cleanup with lifecycle tests.
name: Test Torch / test_torch_ops :: cpu_task

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing the layouts during global optimization makes that phase
target aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding
tensor graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their
epilogues and result unpacks.

Add the experimental --iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling flag. It
takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags, so
conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set, and the
route uses the operation families and encoding strategy of
dispatch-time data tiling.

The route applies to modules with a single llvm-cpu target on x86_64 or
AArch64 that uses the CPU encoding resolver without inner-tiled layouts,
and only with the default encoding strategy. For these modules, global
optimization propagates reshapes, normalizes contraction dimensions,
assigns and propagates encodings, and materializes them on the host. It
then records the target on the module, even if nothing was data-tiled.
Dispatch creation therefore skips encoding assignment for the whole
module, always fuses data-tiled ops with their epilogues and result
unpacks, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions. Other
modules keep dispatch-time data tiling. The enable_inner_tiled check
moves from the CPU encoding models to the Codegen utilities, so that the
eligibility check can share it.

On an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32, median of 10), the route is within
noise of dispatch-time data tiling for a matmul with bias and ReLU, a
batch matmul with ReLU and a convolution with ReLU. x86_64 has not been
measured.

The layout decision is split over several passes, supports one CPU
target per module, and adds HAL and Codegen dependencies to the global
phases. The TODOs describe moving it into its own component that decides
per affinity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: pre-commit

epilogues and result unpacks.

conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set, and the

On an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32, median of 10), the route is within
noise of dispatch-time data tiling for a matmul with bias and ReLU, a
batch matmul with ReLU and a convolution with ReLU. x86_64 has not been
measured.

The layout decision is split over several passes, supports one CPU
target per module, and adds HAL and Codegen dependencies to the global
phases. The TODOs describe moving it into its own component that decides
per affinity.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Preserve the target of materialized tensor layouts

Once tensor layouts have been materialized for a device, dispatch
creation must neither assign encodings to them again nor compile them
for another device. Assigning encodings again re-encodes data-tiled
convolutions when convolutions are data-tiled, and tile shapes chosen
for one CPU can be unsupported or slow on another.

Record the target in a module attribute. Skip dispatch-time encoding
assignment for such modules, and reject them at the start of dispatch
creation when they are compiled for a different target, for several
targets, or for none. Modules without the attribute keep the existing
assignment, now wrapped in a module pass so that no function pass has
to read the attribute. Its options carry the operation families and
encoding strategy, so that printed pipelines and crash reproducers keep
them.

Nothing sets the attribute yet. A follow-up sets it in an experimental
route that materializes layouts during global optimization.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Preserve the target of materialized tensor layouts

Once tensor layouts have been materialized for a device, dispatch
creation must neither assign encodings to them again nor compile them
for another device. Assigning encodings again re-encodes data-tiled
convolutions when convolutions are data-tiled, and tile shapes chosen
for one CPU can be unsupported or slow on another.

Record the target in a module attribute. Skip dispatch-time encoding
assignment for such modules, and reject them at the start of dispatch
creation when they are compiled for a different target, for several
targets, or for none. Modules without the attribute keep the existing
assignment, now wrapped in a module pass so that no function pass has
to read the attribute. Its options carry the operation families and
encoding strategy, so that printed pipelines and crash reproducers keep
them.

Nothing sets the attribute yet. A follow-up sets it in an experimental
route that materializes layouts during global optimization.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fuse packed contractions with epilogues and unpack

When contractions reach dispatch formation already packed, mmt4d ops
are not fused with their elementwise epilogues, and the result unpack
of mmt4d ops and data-tiled convolutions becomes a separate dispatch.

Add opt-in fusion of layout-preserving mmt4d epilogues and of the
result unpack. Epilogues must read the contraction result and write
their own result through identity maps. Only the unpack layouts that
data-tiling materialization produces are matched: row-major mmt4d
results, the transposed narrow-N form, and NHWC, NCHW and unit-batch
HWC convolution results. A group holds pack-like ops or the result

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fuse packed contractions with epilogues and unpack

When contractions reach dispatch formation already packed, mmt4d ops
are not fused with their elementwise epilogues, and the result unpack
of mmt4d ops and data-tiled convolutions becomes a separate dispatch.

Add opt-in fusion of layout-preserving mmt4d epilogues and of the
result unpack. Epilogues must read the contraction result and write
their own result through identity maps. Only the unpack layouts that
data-tiling materialization produces are matched: row-major mmt4d
results, the transposed narrow-N form, and NHWC, NCHW and unit-batch
HWC convolution results. A group holds pack-like ops or the result
unpack, but not both.

The unpack is the last op of its group, so a consumer of a claimed
unpack gets its own dispatch instead of fusing with the unpack. An
unpack that its root does not claim becomes a root at its own position,
as without the options. Other fusion decisions are unchanged.

No pipeline enables the options yet. A follow-up enables them for
modules whose layouts are materialized before dispatch formation.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves and
add a function pass for propagation outside dispatches. Keep the
existing hoisting behavior, and stop at existing dispatches and block
boundaries.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps set_encoding ops with tensor.cast
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
Keep them separate until propagation through generic ops goes through
the encoding propagation interfaces.

Also stop bubbling set_encoding ops whose encoding is not an
EncodingAttr, such as a padding encoding, instead of crashing. Hoisting
already reached this within dispatches.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. A follow-up adds it to an
experimental route that assigns and materializes data-tiling layouts
before dispatch formation.

commit_message:
[Stream] Fix O(N²) compile-time scaling in partitionRegionConcurrency (#24958)

When analyzing execution regions where many operations share a common
resource operand, `partitionRegionConcurrencyReference` previously
invoked `tiedOp.hasAnyTiedUses(operand)` inside the `operand.getUsers()`
loop. Because checking whether an operand has tied uses involves
scanning its use sites, repeating this check inside the loop caused
quadratic $O(N^2)$ traversal over the users of that operand.

This change hoists the check out of the loop using the static helper
`IREE::Util::TiedOpInterface::hasAnyTiedUses(operand)` as an early exit.
Inside the loop, it now only checks whether the candidate user
implements `TiedOpInterface`. This eliminates redundant scans and
resolves the compiler performance bottleneck while preserving existing
partitioning semantics.

Fixes #24928

  Signed-off-by: @isa-Lai 
  Assisted-by:  Gemini CLI

Signed-off-by: isa-lai <isabellai1004@gmail.com>
